paper.citation: Yang, S., Wang, L. and Ding, P. (2019). Causal inference with confounders missing not at random. Biometrika, 106(4), 875-888. DOI: 10.1093/biomet/asz048.
paper.source_locator: Section 5.2, One confounder subject to missingness; journal pages 884-885; electronic PDF reader pages 10-11 of 27. DGP equations are unnumbered prose. Section 2.1 defines ATE and Assumptions 1-2; Section 2.3 defines Assumption 6 (outcome-independent missingness). Supplementary material: 13-page PDF, S1 diagrams, S2 proofs, S3 estimator details, S4 Bayesian estimation; no additional parameter values for Section 5.2 were identified.

mechanism.name: ATE with one confounder subject to nonrandom missingness

generation_equations.label: Missingness indicator
generation_equations.expression: R1 | X1,X2,A ~ Bernoulli(p); logit(p) = -2 + 2*X1 + A*(1.5 + X2); R1=1 means X1 observed

sampling.dependence: Independent and identically distributed full-data individuals. Within an individual, X1 and X2 affect treatment, potential outcomes and the missingness indicator. R1 is generated conditional on A and the complete X; observed X1 is masked according to R1. No interference or clustering.

assumptions: Consistency: observed outcome Y = A Y(1) + (1-A)Y(0).

Conditional exchangeability in the full data: {Y(0),Y(1)} independent of A conditional on X=(X1,X2), as Assumption 1 in Section 2.1 states; this follows from the declared simulator convention of independent potential-outcome errors conditional on X and the treatment law depending only on X.

Pointwise treatment positivity from the logistic assignment law. With the stated unbounded Gaussian support, a uniform bound c1 <= P(A=1|X) <= c2 as in Assumption 2 is not established and in fact cannot hold globally for this logistic form.
Outcome-independent missingness: R1 is independent of Y conditional on (A,X), consistent with Assumption 6. R1 may depend on the missing confounder X1 itself, so the missingness is not at random.

Full-data individuals are iid as described in Section 2.2. X1-X2 joint independence and cross-independence of potential-outcome errors are implementation conventions, not fully specified in the Section 5.2 paragraph, and require scientific confirmation.

Assumption 7 in Section 2.3 requires a uniform positive lower bound on the probability of complete observation. With unbounded X1 and the stated missingness logit, no such uniform lower bound is guaranteed. Assumption 8 (bounded completeness) also needs separate mathematical review. The known analytic oracle does not by itself establish identification assumptions for estimators.

properties.notes: Only two baseline covariates, so not high-dimensional. The missingness logit has the explicit interaction A*(1.5+X2), which expands to 1.5*A + A*X2. Logistic links appear in treatment and missingness models. X1 is stored as 0.0 when R1=0 because the collection interface rejects non-finite numeric cells; use R1 to distinguish a missing X1 from an observed zero.

estimand.name: ATE = E[Y(1)-Y(0)]
estimand.definition: Population average effect of intervening to set treatment A from 0 (control) to 1 (active), averaged over the full pre-treatment covariate distribution before missingness: E[Y(1)-Y(0)].

parameters.source_section: Section 5.2, One confounder subject to missingness
parameters.joint_law_convention: Independent X1 and X2 for executable candidate; Section 5.2 gives marginals but no explicit joint-dependence statement. Pending confirmation.
parameters.potential_outcome_error_convention: epsilon0 and epsilon1 drawn independently of each other and X; marginals are source-defined, cross-independence is an implementation convention pending confirmation.
parameters.positivity_review_note: On unbounded Gaussian support, logistic treatment and missingness probabilities are pointwise in (0,1) but no uniform lower/upper bounds follow; formal Assumptions 2 and 7 need scientific review.

truth.expression: Population average effect of intervening to set treatment A from 0 (control) to 1 (active), averaged over the full pre-treatment covariate distribution before missingness: E[Y(1)-Y(0)].
truth.derivation: Analytic coefficient contrast. Y(1)-Y(0)=-0.5 + X1 + X2 + epsilon(1)-epsilon(0); using E[X1]=1, E[X2]=0.5 and zero-mean errors gives ATE=1. The numerical error is zero conditional on the stated error mean assumptions.

adaptations: Section 5.2 specifies the marginal laws X1 ~ Normal(1,1) and X2 ~ Bernoulli(0.5), but does not explicitly state their joint dependence. For the executable candidate, X1 and X2 are generated independently; the paper's approximate 67% response-rate report is consistent with this convention but does not uniquely prove it. Maintainer/scientific confirmation is requested.

The paper specifies marginal laws epsilon(0) ~ Normal(0,1) and epsilon(1) ~ Normal(0,1), but Section 5.2 does not state all cross-independence relations. The executable implementation draws the errors independently of each other and X; this extra joint-law convention remains pending scientific confirmation.

The collection worker accepts only finite numeric observed columns. To preserve the missingness pattern without NaN/Inf output, the exported X1 column uses 0.0 as a sentinel when R1=0 and exports R1 explicitly; when R1=1, X1 retains its generated value. This is an interface encoding, not an imputation, and must be interpreted jointly with R1.
Use analytic ATE truth and CPU smoke checks instead of reproducing the paper's full 2,000-replicate simulation study, 100 imputed datasets, or 500-replicate bootstrap variance calculations.
